variants.note: massing_affinities: 'picturesque irregularity destroys the only compositional rule the style has.'

composition_parti.rule_append: Renaissance Revival is on the strict-bilateral institutional side of the family's split (c01): the principal elevation is exactly symmetrical about the entrance axis, with no projecting bay, tower, or wing permitted to break it.

If the roof is a visible storey, it is Second Empire.'

roof_form.rule: A low side-gable roof whose ridge runs between the party walls, concealed behind the continuous crowning cornice of the row; a hip only at the end of a row.
roof_form.note: BOUND 1 Oct 2026 (WP-16.9), on Lucas's answer B12 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/the-roof-is-drawn-side-gabled-whatever-the-style-says: renaissance-revival-american binds its own roof_form. Until then the slot was open and resolved ITALIANATE-AMERICAN's record, `low-hip-suppressed` canonical, a free-standing house's roof, so the roof layer drew this party-wall row house hipped. Its canonical massings are the townhouse row and the side-hall double pile. Marked judgment: the record names its party walls and its continuous cornice, not a roof id.

variants.note: Diagnostic tell: sawn brackets, not modillions or dentils, signal Italianate, not Renaissance Revival.

eave_condition.rule: The eave is terminated by the modillioned or dentilled crowning cornice, never by sawn brackets — the fastest distinguishing tell against Italianate.

cornice_return.rule: No cornice return: the crowning cornice runs unbroken across the full width of the facade and across party walls.
cornice_return.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), on Lucas's answer A4 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/an-inherited-ban-decides-what-the-elevation-may-draw (WP-16.2 stage 2): each of the Italianate family binds its own cornice return forbidden, on its own roof. Until then it was forbidden by GOTHIC-REVIVAL-AMERICAN, on 'The rake is finished in bargeboard, not a boxed classical cornice with mitred returns; a cornice return signals Greek Revival millwork, not Gothic Revival (see distinguished_from).' -- a bargeboarded rake, which is not this style's. This record states no roof form and no gable; its cornice is a party-wall cornice: c03 reads 'shall run unbroken across the full width of the facade, including across party walls in a row.' Marked judgment, because the record names no gable end and the ban is read from the cornice it does state.

storey_diminish_pct.note: Equivalent to c02's 'each storey 78 to 88 percent of the one below', restated as diminish-percentage.

height_proportion.rule: Floor-to-floor heights diminish monotonically upward, each storey between 78 and 88 percent of the one below, with the piano nobile at least 1.15 times the storey above it (c02). 'The only style in this branch that is' genuinely proportional in the storey-height sense.

variants.note: Defining_characteristics, verbatim: 'a wooden Renaissance Revival is a contradiction.'
Same fact; no wood-frame register exists for this style.

construction_type.rule_append: Masonry only: ashlar, brownstone, pressed brick, or cast iron. Every frame variant the family otherwise permits is forbidden here.

variants.note: The commercial register: 'a catalogue of columns, arches, spandrels, and cornices, orderable by number, assembled in weeks.'
Defining_characteristics, verbatim: 'a wooden Renaissance Revival is a contradiction.'
Same: no wood cladding of any kind in this masonry style.

primary_cladding.rule: Ashlar, brownstone, pressed brick, or cast iron; a wooden Renaissance Revival is a contradiction.

belt_course.rule: Flat, uninterrupted wall plane articulated by string courses and quoins rather than by projection.

corner_quoin.rule: Quoins run the full height of the corner from water table to cornice in an unbroken alternating rhythm, long faces 18 to 30 in. Partial-height or purely decorative quoining is prohibited (c05).

variants.note: Diagnostic tell, verbatim: that would be Italianate.

cornice.rule: A single dominant crowning cornice, modillioned or dentilled, terminating the wall against the sky, projecting 1/16 to 1/12 of total facade height and running unbroken across the full width including party walls (c03).

variants.note: Italianate's signature, not this style's; storey heads here are classical pediments/entablatures, not arches.

window_type.rule: Window heads are differentiated by storey — typically pedimented or entablatured below, square-headed above — never round-arched.

alternation_closure.value: an alternating pediment sequence begins and ends with the same type so the row reads as closed

window_head_masonry.rule: Window head treatment changes at each storey and is uniform within a storey. Where alternating pediments are used, the alternation begins and ends with the same type (c04).

window_head_wood.note: Masonry-only style; 'a wooden Renaissance Revival is a contradiction.'

window_grouping_rule.rule: Three, five, or seven bays at equal spacing, with the centre bay optionally widened by not more than 15 percent.

variants.note: This style's own kit: 'Astylar: no engaged pilaster order either; enrichment is confined to window surrounds and the cornice', and defining_characteristics[1]: 'Astylar composition: no columns, no portico, no pediment on the facade as a whole'.

door_surround.rule: No pilaster-and-entablature doorcase: the composition is astylar, and enrichment is confined to the window surrounds and the cornice.
door_surround.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), on Lucas's answer A4 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/an-inherited-ban-decides-what-the-elevation-may-draw (WP-16.2 stage 2): each of the Italianate family binds its own door surround, forbidding the pilaster-and-entablature doorcase in its own record's words. Until then it resolved GOTHIC-REVIVAL-BRITISH's whole record, whose rule reads 'A projecting, gabled and buttressed porch with a pointed arch and hood mould -- never a classical pilaster-and-entablature doorcase (hard constraint c05).' -- so a pointed-arch buttressed porch was canonical here and the pilaster doorcase was refused for c05's reason, not this style's. The ban was right here in outcome and wrong in reason: this style's own kit and defining_characteristics[1], quoted in this record, rule the pilaster out. The record does name a door surround, and an enriched one: its palladio-composite note has the order govern 'the enrichment of the window aedicules, the door surround, and the crowning cornice's modillion/dentil profile' (proportion_packs[0]), and its opening-proportion note speaks of 'whatever surround the primary order supplies' (proportion_packs[4]). No variant id in use states that astylar surround, so none is stated here. Lucas's answer adds that where the doorcase is refused the elevation draws the plain casing; that refusal is WP-16.4's and is not built, and a plain casing is less than the enriched surround proportion_packs[0] names.

transom_sidelight.rule: No fanlight and no sidelights: enrichment is confined to the window surrounds and the cornice.
transom_sidelight.note: BOUND 30 Sep 2026 (WP-16.2), on Lucas's answer A4 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/an-inherited-ban-decides-what-the-elevation-may-draw (WP-16.2 stage 2): renaissance-revival-american forbids the fanlight and the sidelights in its own kit's words. Until then it was FORBIDDEN whole, inherited on 'EDITORIAL: not directly documented either way; forbidden on the strength of c05's general prohibition rather than a direct quotation about fanlights specifically.' from GOTHIC-REVIVAL-BRITISH. This record never names the entrance's glazing. Its own kit confines enrichment to the window surrounds and the cornice, and the answer reads that as ruling out the fanlight and the sidelights. The record is not of one mind: its palladio-composite note lists 'the door surround' among what the order enriches (proportion_packs[0]). The answer names the fanlight and the sidelights and not the transom, and the record names none of them, so the rectangular transom is left unstated rather than guessed. Marked judgment for these reasons. With the whole-slot ban replaced the cascade dimensions the slot all the same: no `packs` block is stated, so precedence gives the address to `opening-mullioned`, bound on jacobean (`0.66`, a bare ratio placing a mullioned window's transom bar up its opening, not the rectangular transom this record leaves unstated), over this node's own `opening-proportion` (the sidelight width, `module / 3`, and the transom height above the door, `module * 0.44`) -- OQ 51's delivery, counted and not endorsed, where the whole-slot ban had shielded it.

variants.note: palladio-composite: the branch's most literally classical node.
vignola-corinthian: the plainer bank or smaller-house register.
Astylar: 'no columns, no portico, no pediment on the facade as a whole' (defining_characteristics).

order.rule: The order supplies the profile family for the cornice's modillion/dentil course and the window aedicules — the enrichment of what IS built — without ever being expressed as a freestanding column, since the composition is astylar.

column.note: Defining_characteristics, verbatim: 'astylar composition: no columns, no portico, no pediment on the facade as a whole.'

variants.note: Astylar; no portico exists to carry one.

entablature.rule: The bound order (see `order`) governs the moulding profile applied to the crowning cornice and the window surrounds, never a portico entablature.

variants.note: Diagnostic tell: 'a Renaissance signature and appears in no other American style of the period.'
Defining_characteristics: 'no pediment on the facade as a whole.'

pediment.rule: Pediments appear over individual window heads, alternating triangular and segmental in a row, never as a single pediment crowning the whole facade.

pilaster.note: Astylar: no engaged pilaster order either; enrichment is confined to window surrounds and the cornice (see `order`, `entablature`).

modillion_dentil.rule: A single dominant crowning cornice, modillioned or dentilled (defining_characteristics; diagnostic tell against Italianate's sawn brackets).

parlour_ceiling_ft.note: OQ 19: independent of the determiner, and necessarily so. `height_proportion` states RATIOS -- storey diminution 12-22%, piano nobile at least 1.15 of the storey above, a rusticated base at 0.8-1.0 -- and a set of ratios cannot yield a height without an anchor. This is the anchor: the ratios are applied from the parlour floor upward and downward.

ceiling_height_rule.rule: Interior ceiling heights follow the exterior storey graduation directly; the double-parlour floor runs fourteen-foot ceilings and eleven-foot windows to the floor.

trim_family.rule: The pedestal:field:entablature wall division is the direct interior counterpart of the astylar exterior order bound above; well inside the trim-classical pack's calibrated range at this style's ceiling heights.
